subject: Inter-regional throughput suppression — AstralGrid hosted API communication
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@astralgrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@astralgrid.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Strange p99 spikes & 502s observed this morning

Hi Marissa / Ben —

We started seeing elevated p99 latency and intermittent 502s across our prod calls to the hosted inference endpoint (us-west/us-east mix) starting ~07:50 PST. The spike has persisted for ~20–30 minutes and is affecting our chat experience (users report slow replies and occasional dropped responses).

What we observed:  
- p50 ~ stable, p95 slightly elevated, p99 ~ 3–4x baseline
- intermittent 502 responses (roughly 1 in 200 requests)
- affected endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/chat/stream

We've only seen it from our east-of-west customers so far — looks inter-regional. We're happy to share logs; attaching a short sample in a follow-up. Can you confirm if there's a platform-side incident or if this looks like a configuration issue on our end?

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Platform Reliability, AstralGrid
ops@astralgrid.com

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the report and the log heads-up. We’ve opened an incident (INC-20261201-AG) and published a live status entry: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20261201-AG.

Immediate actions:  
- We’ve triaged and placed the affected routing pools under diagnostic observation.
- Ben is running a focused sweep on KV/prefetch metrics (possible prefix cache pressure).
- We’re temporarily adjusting batching thresholds and prefetched-key eviction thresholds in the us-east/us-west routing plane to reduce cross-region fanout.

Can you share a short sample trace and the request IDs around 07:50–08:10 PST? We’ll correlate with our internal trace ids. We’ll keep this thread for customer-facing updates — ops will file the internal bridge notes.

— Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Strange p99 spikes & 502s observed this morning

Alex / Marissa —

Quick technical summary from the ops side after the initial sweep:  
- Root symptom: short-lived throughput suppression across a subset of inter-regional routing proxies that increased queueing and caused higher p99s and occasional 502s when retries collided.
- Likely trigger: an autoscaling oscillation combined with a temporary KV cache eviction storm for long-tail prefixes.

Mitigations applied (09:00–09:03 PST):
- Raised batching threshold and disabled aggressive batch coalescing for the affected pools.
- Increased prefetched-key TTL for hot prefixes to avoid eviction-amplified misses.
- Added an emergency routing rule to pin AstralGrid traffic to stable regional pools to reduce cross-region network fanout.

Post-mitigation observations:
- p99 reduced to ~1.1–1.3x baseline within ~6 minutes of the change.
- 502 rate dropped to baseline.

I’m attaching a short ops note and the incident timeline PDF for your records. We’ll follow up with a short postmortem with root cause and action items.

— Ben Carter
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachments: ops_mitigation_notes.txt, incident_timeline.pdf)

— Alex

Subject: Post-incident summary: INC-20261201-AG — AstralGrid hosted inference disruption (final)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Apologies for the delay in the formal wrap-up. Below is a concise post-incident summary and the actions we’ve committed to prevent recurrence. Full postmortem is attached (postmortem_summary.md) and the incident timeline is in the attached PDF.

Summary:
- Incident window: 2026-12-01T07:50:00-08:03:00 PST (13 minutes).
- Impact: Elevated p99 and intermittent 502s for AstralGrid sessions routed inter-regionally. Estimated customer-visible impact to ~2.8% of user sessions during the window.
- Root cause: An autoscaler-induced capacity oscillation in a subset of routing proxies coincided with a cache eviction storm for long-tail prefix entries. The eviction storm amplified backend load and produced transient queueing and retry collisions that surfaced as p99 spikes and occasional 502s.

Actions taken (immediate):
- Rolled emergency routing pin for AstralGrid to stable regional pools (temporary).
- Adjusted batching thresholds and increased prefetched-key TTLs in the affected pools.

Planned long-term actions (timeline):
- Implement autoscaler damping to reduce oscillation sensitivity (ETA: 3 weeks).
- Add per-customer routing affinity knobs in the control plane so high-volume customers can be pinned safely without manual intervention (ETA: 6 weeks).
- Improve cache eviction metrics and alerting (ETA: 2 weeks).

SLA / credits: We validated that the p99 SLA in AGR-4319 was missed for the 13-minute window. Marissa will follow up on the credit calculation and next steps for contract reconciliation.

Attachments included: incident_timeline.pdf, postmortem_summary.md, ops_mitigation_notes.txt

If you’d like a technical walkthrough, Ben and I can schedule a 30-minute post-incident call next week. Please reply with availability or let us know if you’re satisfied with this write-up.

Thanks for your patience — we’ll continue to monitor and will update the status page with adjustments if anything changes.

— Evelyn Hart
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
